attempts.summary: Configured DHCP relay so node3 obtains its address from node2's DHCP service across node1's two segmented interfaces. node1 (SONiC/Debian) got eth1=172.20.1.1/24 (node2's segment) and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 (node3's segment) with isc-dhcp-relay forwarding between them and IP forwarding enabled. node2 got isc-dhcp-server installed, configured to serve range 172.20.2.100-200 for node3's subnet, listening on ens7=172.20.1.2/24. Root-caused a silent failure where dhcpd's unicast reply to the relay's giaddr (172.20.2.1) was being sent out node2's management default route instead of via node1, by adding a static route 172.20.2.0/24 via 172.20.1.1 on node2. Verified node3 obtains a full DHCP lease (DISCOVER/OFFER/REQUEST/ACK) via dhclient. All configuration was persisted (interfaces.d files, sysctl.d, enabled systemd services) and validated to survive a full reboot of each node in sequence (node1, then node2, then node3), including node3 automatically re-acquiring its DHCP-assigned address from node2 through node1's relay purely from boot-time networking, with no manual intervention.
